html:
On 6 September 2018 the Supreme Court of India ruled that consensual sex between adults of the same sex is not a crime. The case is Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India.

The law at issue was Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code, written under British rule in 1860, which punished "carnal intercourse against the order of nature". Britain spread similar laws across its empire. In 2009 the Delhi High Court had read it down in the Naz Foundation case, but in 2013 the Supreme Court restored it.

Five judges ruled unanimously in 2018 that the law violated the rights to equality, dignity and privacy in the Constitution of India. The ruling was celebrated across India and studied in other former British colonies with the same law. It did not give same sex couples the right to marry; in 2023 the court left that question to Parliament. Compare Taiwan, the first in Asia to allow it.
sum: On 6 September 2018 the Supreme Court of India ruled that consensual sex between adults of the same sex is not a crime. The case is Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India.
